source_claim_versions.exact_statement: FEI is exists finite C, for every finite n and every Boolean sign f, H2(f)<=C I(f), including constants with H=I=0. The 37 inventoried manuscript interfaces separate proper-class theorems, one-way sufficient payments and proved equivalences; no audited interface establishes finiteness of C_FEI.
source_claim_versions.first_unproved_line: A dimension-independent payment for the universal posterior residual, hereditary erasure selection, gate potential, or actual-source history remains unpaid; see each route separately.

source_claim_versions.exact_statement: Fix any actual Boolean F0(X,Y0) on disjoint finite input groups and its X spectral marginal. Among Boolean functions with that fixed marginal and admitting fresh arbitrary data tensor factors, the optimal constant in H(S_Y|S_X)<=C I equals C_FEI as an extended-real supremum. Any fixed upper X-degree bound obeyed by F0 is preserved by the embedding.

For every integer m>=1, f_m=2*1[x0=1]*1[at least one xi=1 for 1<=i<=m]-1 on the uniform (m+1)-cube, represented as the union of the m distinct clauses (x0 AND xi), with supports ordered (0,i), M_i=1, pi_i=1/4 and lambda_i=1/m, has exact finite posterior partition weights S_B({0})=1/4, S_B(T)=m^(-t)*(a/4)^t, and S_B({0} union T)=t!*a^(t-1)/(4*m^t)*(1+(1-t/m)*a), where t=|T|>=1 and a=2^(-6/5). Its complete conditioned all-partition residual is <=(43/10) I(f_m), and its exact conditioned all-partition run-cost expectation is <=(23/2) I(f_m). A normalized prior w_k=1/((k+1)(k+2)) on lambda_i^(k)=2^(-k)/m pays at most v additional bits, giving bounds (53/10) I and (25/2) I respectively. Every point-mass posterior choice in this representation has residual/I tending to infinity as m tends to infinity.

source_claim_versions.exact_statement: For every finite uniform selector decision tree with no repeated query along any path and Boolean leaves on an independent common data cube, given complete leaf spectral prefix codes of expected costs c_l, there is a constructive cover C_l AND [g_l=1] and an exact joint spectral witness with a prefix code of expected cost 2D+sum_l p_l c_l, where p_l=2^(-d_l) and D=sum_l p_l d_l. If I_sel(F)>=gamma D and c_l<=K I(g_l), this full cost is <=max(2/gamma,K) I(F). For unsigned nonempty character leaves with repeated labels allowed, the leaf costs are zero and I_sel=B/2, where B=E_x sum_j 1[label(x)!=label(x^flip_j)]; B>=beta D gives full cost <=(4/beta) I_sel. The alternating two-label first-positive comb has D=2(1-2^(-a)), B>=D/2, I_data=1 and I_sel<1 for every a>=1, hence full cost <=8 I_sel while conjunction-cover read and a are unbounded.

For every integer a>=0, ordinary fresh addressing with 2^a distinct data bits has H=2a and I=1+a/2. Under the explicit fixed code and queue definitions in REPORT.md, the repeated-label complete code has expected cost a(2+a/2), the optimal whole-set code and its singleton posterior cost 2a, and the source fractional pressure equals (7/2)a^2+(11/5)a. Their cost/I asymptotics are a+2+o(1), 4, and 7a+O(1), respectively. The literal one-root original queue and the conditioned singleton-posterior queue have common limiting cost/I=2+2G, with G defined by the integral in REPORT.md section 5 and 4<=2+2G<=4+(6/5)(1-1/(2 ln 2)). The coarse forest residual/I tends to 16/5; the complete coarse forest RHS/I tends to K_ref+16/5. All partition-posterior optima and unrestricted FEI are outside this claim.

source_claim_versions.exact_statement: For every balanced Boolean b, integers t,k>=1, q=2^-k and c=1/ln2, F=1+A_k(product_{j=1}^t b_j-1) has H(F)=q[tH(b)+4k+2c]-q^2(2k+3c)+R(q), I(F)=q[tI(b)+k], and -2cq^3/[3(1-q)]<=R(q)<=0. The exact entropy is q t H(b)+(4q-2q^2)k-2(1-q)^2 log2(1-q); variance is 2q-q^2 and minority probability q/2. If k=o(t) and 2^-k t->0 for a fixed seed, H(F)/I(F)->H(b)/I(b) with influence tending to zero.

For the same family, a control-first stopping tree has terminal entropy 2^-k t H(b), queried influence k2^-k, and exact magnitude-mismatch/KL debt J_tree=2^-k(k+A_k). Here A_k=sum_{s=1}^k 2^-s[2s-1+log2(1-2^(1-s)+2^(1-2s))] and there exists A in [0,3] with 0<=A-A_k<=(2k+3)2^-k. Hence J_tree<=2^-k(k+3)<=4k2^-k uniformly in tensor count. The blind rarity sum before KL subtraction is 2^-k k(k+1)/2. At each active node s, mu=2^-s and J_s=mu-mu^2+mu^2 log2((1-2mu+2mu^2)/mu^2).

Every nonconstant uniform-cube Boolean sign function with nonzero Fourier support of affine F2 dimension at most four, and every disjoint product of such factors, has a relevant physical coordinate i with B_i <= (7/2) I_i. This class is closed under physical restrictions and satisfies H <= (7/2+2/ln 2) I.

source_claim_versions.exact_statement: For f=+1 exactly at Hamming weights >=24 on 32 uniform sign bits, every coordinate has edge amplitude proxy A_i=2 sum_T |fhat(T) fhat(T+i)| with A_i/I_i=2220940451/536870912>4. Thus existential proxy selection with K=4 is false. No true-erasure violation or unbounded-ratio family is claimed.

For every finite uniform-cube Boolean sign f, let a_S=fhat(S), p_S=a_S^2, ell_S=log2(1/p_S) on positive atoms and a_S ell_S=0 otherwise, c_U=sum_S a_S a_(S xor U) ell_S, E_log=sum_(U nonempty)|U|c_U^2, and J_R=sum_(U nonempty)p_(R xor U)/|U|. Every occupied R obeys p_R[H(f)-ell_R]^2<=J_R E_log; also sum_(U nonempty)c_U^2=Var_p(ell). For a largest atom, H(f)<=ell_R+sqrt(J_R E_log/p_R).

There is no finite universal K with E_log(f)<=K I(f), nor any finite universal K with sqrt(J_R E_log(f)/p_R)<=K I(f) for the largest-atom anchor R of every Boolean f. The first is refuted by n-bit one-point defects with E_log/I~4n^2; the second by disjoint tensor powers of the three-bit point defect, whose anchor cost is exponentially large while influence is linear.

For the actual Boolean sign g(x,y)=(-1)^(xy) on independent Bernoulli inputs with P(X=1)=p and fixed P(Y=1)=q in (0,1/2), and physical reveal A={X}, the Shannon spectral/physical-channel quantities satisfy J_A-M_A=4q(1-2q)*p*log2(1/p)+O_q(p) as p tends to zero. Consequently every scalar tau(p) such that J_A<=M_A+tau(p) for all finite actual Boolean signs under every interior product bias and every singleton block of bias p satisfies liminf_{p->0} tau(p)/(p*log2(1/p))>=1/2. In particular no universal O(p) tax is valid. This does not refute B09 Delta(p), prove its optimality, or disprove uniform-cube FEI.

For actual Boolean signs on finite uniform cubes with entropy in bits, let C_* be the extended supremum of H/I over nonconstants. Fixed-dimensional maxima M_n exist, increase to C_*, and satisfy M_n<=n*2^(n-1). For every finite 0<=C<C_*, there exists a witness H>CI of least essential physical dimension; such witnesses approximate C_* along thresholds approaching C_* (or increasing to infinity). Disjoint tensor products add H,I,D_C and violating products have a violating factor. Balancing k tensor copies gives deficit kD_C-C. Balanced singleton activation has H=pH(g)+2rp(2-p)+h((1-p)^2), I=p(I(g)+r). For every nonconstant f, the activated balanced sequence k=m^2,r=m has R tending to R(f) with I and minority probability tending to zero. These operations preserve threshold admission after sufficient amplification but do not generally preserve dimension-criticality; arbitrary restriction need not preserve H/I. No global optimizer attainment is asserted.

Fix finite C>=0 and an actual Boolean dimension-critical C-witness f, meaning H(f)>CI(f) and its essential physical dimension is minimal among all such witnesses. Every proper physical restriction has deficit D_C<=0, and f has no proper nonconstant disjoint tensor factorization. For every nonempty block A of its essential coordinates, L_A-CI_A>=D_C(f)>0, with L_A=H(f)-E H(f_a)=H(Z_A|Z_Ac)+I(a;T), where a is uniform and T is sampled from the actual child Fourier spectrum. Every finite adaptive physical restriction tree satisfies D_C(f)=sum_internal pi_v(L_v-Cd_v)+sum_leaves pi_lD_C(f_l); with proper leaves the internal sum is at least D_C(f). No component-pruning, connectedness, or inherited descendant-criticality conclusion is asserted.

For every Boolean outer gate h and Boolean children g_i on mutually disjoint uniform physical blocks, after absorbing constant children, with m_i=E g_i, v_i=1-m_i^2>0, a_mu the output-product orthonormal Fourier coefficients and w_i=sum_{T containing i} a_mu(T)^2, E F=E_mu h, Var F=Var_mu h, H(F)=H_mu(h)+sum_i (w_i/v_i)(H(g_i)-h2(v_i)), and Inf_x(F)=(w_i/v_i)Inf_x(g_i) for x in block i. Balanced children specialize to H(F)=H(h)+sum_i Inf_i(h)H(g_i) and I(F)=sum_i Inf_i(h)I(g_i).

At every fixed physical restriction, disjoint composition identities hold with newly restricted children, absorbed constants, and the outer gate reexpanded under the new child-output product law. Balance before restriction does not imply balance afterwards. For AND_2 composed with majority_3(x,a,b) and dictator z, fixing x=+1 gives E F=-1/4, I(F)=5/4, H(F)=4-(9/8)log2(3), whereas retaining the initial balanced outer law predicts -1/2, 1, and 3 respectively.

For every finite-dimensional uniform Boolean sign and fair adaptive physical restriction policy querying each coordinate at most once, with filtration given by past physical observations and an independent policy seed, H(g_t)+sum_{s<t}D_s and I(g_t)+sum_{s<t}d_s are stopped martingales, where D_s=B_s+J_s is the conditional spectral erasure plus the actual physical-child/spectral mutual information and d_s is queried influence. For tau<=n, H(f)=E H(g_tau)+E sum_{s<tau}D_s and I(f)=E I(g_tau)+E sum_{s<tau}d_s.

On every such fair finite tree, lambda_t=sum_{T:b_T^2>0}b_T^2 log2((a_T^2+b_T^2)/b_T^2) satisfies D_t<=lambda_t+(3/ln(2))d_t. Therefore (3/ln(2))I(g_t)-H(g_t)-sum_{s<t}lambda_s is a supermartingale. If at every live node every positive b_T^2/(a_T^2+b_T^2)>=epsilon for fixed epsilon in (0,1], then C I(g_t)-H(g_t) is a supermartingale for C=log2(1/epsilon)+3/ln(2); hence H(f)<=C I(f)+E[H(g_tau)-C I(g_tau)].

For every Boolean sign f on every finite uniform cube, with p_S=hat(f)(S)^2, I=sum |S|p_S, H_nat=sum p_S ln(1/p_S), T_t=exp(-tL), L chi_S=|S|chi_S, q_t(S)=p_S exp(-2t|S|), G_f(t)=sum q_t(S)ln(1/p_S) and J_f(t)=sum |S|q_t(S)ln(1/p_S), G_f prime=-2J_f and H_nat=p_empty ln(1/p_empty)+2 integral_0^infinity J_f. The boundary term is between zero and I; J_f(t)<=J_f(0) and J_f(t)<=exp(-2t)J_f(0), giving integrability at both endpoints for every fixed f. For n>=1, J_f(0)<=2(n-1)ln(2)I. A universal integral bound integral J_f<=KI implies FEI in bits with constant (1+2K)/ln(2), and FEI with bit constant C implies that integral bound with K=C ln(2)/2.

There is no nonnegative measurable k with finite integral on (0,infinity) such that J_f(t)<=I(f)k(t) for every finite-dimensional Boolean sign f and almost every t. For f_n(x)=1-2 indicator{x=(1,...,1)}, n>=2, J_f_n(t)/I(f_n)=(2n-2)ln(2)exp(-2t)((1+exp(-2t))/2)^(n-1). Any such pointwise envelope must be at least ln(2)exp(-3/2)/t almost everywhere on (0,1/4]. Nevertheless integral J_f_n/I(f_n)=2(1-1/n)(1-2^(-n))ln(2)<=2ln(2). This refutes the integrable pointwise-envelope helper, not the integrated target or FEI.

new_claims.exact_statement: For every fixed finite residual cube with a fixed interior product measure and fixed Boolean sign children G,H, let X be independent Bernoulli(p), F_p=G when X=1 and H when X=0, M_p=H(S_X|S_residual) and J_p=I(X;T) in the physical-child/spectral experiment, in bits. If a=hat G,b=hat H,D=support(b),A=sum_D a_T^2,c=E[GH], then J_p-M_p=2(c-A)p log2(1/p)+O_{G,H,measure}(p), and 1/2-2(c-A)=2||P_D a-c b||_2^2+2(c-1/2)^2. Therefore -4<=2(c-A)<=1/2, and the supremum over fixed actual Boolean pairs of the limiting coefficient equals 1/2. Equality holds exactly when c=1/2 and P_D a=b/2, realized by H=1,G=(-1)^(y1*y2) on two uniform residual bits. No dimension-uniform remainder or exchange of supremum and limit is asserted.

new_claims.exact_statement: For every finite Boolean sign under any interior product measure, any singleton physical block X with bias p, and Shannon entropy in bits, let M_X=H(S_X|S_residual), J_X=I(X;T) in the actual physical-child/spectral experiment, r=min(p,1-p), and delta=1-sqrt(1-r). Then J_X-M_X<=h2(r)-h2(delta). The bound is uniform in dimension, residual biases and Boolean children. Consequently lim_{p->0} sup_{all finite actual Boolean signs and all interior residual product biases}(J_X-M_X)/(p log2(1/p))=1/2. The tax expansion is (r/2)log2(1/r)+((log2(e)-1)/2)r+O(r^2 log(1/r)); exact optimal tax at arbitrary nonzero p and influence/composition payment remain unproved.
